taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: flowering stems 15 cm to 50 cm tall in subalpine meadows, as in the photos; Abrams and Ferris (1960 p. 346): up to 7 dm.

traits.height_max_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 346, Erigeron peregrinus: fibrous-rooted perennial from a short rhizome or short stout caudex, up to 7 dm. tall.

traits.life_span.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 346, Erigeron peregrinus: fibrous-rooted perennial.

traits.woodiness.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 346, Erigeron peregrinus: fibrous-rooted perennial, amply leafy.

traits.leaf_habit.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: the leaves die back each winter.

traits.perennation.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 346, Erigeron peregrinus: from a short rhizome or short stout caudex.

traits.rhizome_habit.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 346, Erigeron peregrinus: from a short rhizome.

traits.rosette.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 346, Erigeron peregrinus: basal and lower cauline leaves well developed, the others smaller.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 20 p. 328, 329 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Erigeron glacialis: basal blades linear-oblanceolate to broadly lanceolate or spatulate, (20-)30-160(-200) x 7-45 mm.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 20 p. 328, 329 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Erigeron glacialis: basal blades (20-)30-160(-200) x 7-45 mm.

traits.petiole_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: the basal blades tapering to a petiole 2 cm to 8 cm long; the upper leaves sessile (Abrams and Ferris 1960 p. 346), so set from 0.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 346, Erigeron peregrinus: linear-oblanceolate to broadly oblanceolate or spatulate blade tapering to the petiole; the key (p. 347): var. callianthemus basal leaves oblanceolate or broader.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 347, Erigeron peregrinus subsp. callianthemus (now E. glacialis): leaves ordinarily entire (key to subspecies).

traits.leaf_hairs.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 347, Erigeron peregrinus subsp. callianthemus (now E. glacialis): herbage usually glabrous except for the closely villous peduncles (key to subspecies).

traits.inflorescence.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 346, Erigeron peregrinus: heads solitary or few; drawn solitary, as most of the photos show.

traits.capitulum_kind.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 346, Erigeron peregrinus: rays 30-80 around a disk.

traits.involucre_diameter_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 346, Erigeron peregrinus: the disk 10-25 mm. wide.

traits.involucre_height_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 346, Erigeron peregrinus: involucre 7-11 mm. high.

traits.ray_florets.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 346, Erigeron peregrinus: rays 30-80; mostly 30 to 60 in the photos.

traits.ray_length_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 346, Erigeron peregrinus: rays 8-25 mm. long.

traits.ray_width_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 346, Erigeron peregrinus: rays 2-4 mm. wide.

traits.ray_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 20 p. 328, 329 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Erigeron glacialis: ray corollas usually blue to rose purple or pink, sometimes white to pale blue; Abrams and Ferris (1960 p. 346) for subsp. callianthemus: rays commonly rich rose-purple or darker. A mid rose-lavender in sRGB, in place of the paler shade first chosen.

traits.disc_colour.note: Disk yellow; sRGB by eye, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 170359193, 179690944, 236536741, 888138, 90781364, 40722067, 17810429, 32412747): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.fruit_type.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 346, Erigeron peregrinus: achenes asymmetrically 4-7-nerved; pappus of 20-30 bristles.

traits.flowering_months.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 346, Erigeron peregrinus: (June) July-Aug.

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: achenes ripe August and September.

appearance.note: By eye, from the photos the traits cite: a tuft of smooth, narrow, spoon-shaped basal leaves with leafy stems each topped by a single daisy of many slender lavender-pink rays around a yellow disk. The basal leaves' petiole share is set by hand from the leaf and petiole lengths the traits give, as no rule sets a rosette leaf's.

generator.params.note: Set by hand for subalpine daisy from its sources and the photos the traits cite: the herb program's structure (stems, nodes, basal leaves, how the flowers are borne). The rest of its growth comes from the library's rules for the form. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 0.3 m tall at 4 years in the open, within its sources' range, as grown. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

sources.title: Project After contributors: hand-set species values
sources.licence: project contribution under the repository's terms

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy added for the Mount Rainier subalpine meadow scene (Paradise, 2026-10-19): sizes and forms from Abrams (vols. 2 to 4) and the Range Plant Handbook where it treats the species, counts and colours from iNaturalist photos.
